prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: מערכת שעות כיתת י'2 – סמסטר א' (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "ראשון" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שני" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שלישי" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "יום" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 2: header "שעה" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 89px
  col 3: header "מקצוע" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 63px
  col 4: header "מורה" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "חדר" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 76px
  col 6: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 64px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A Hebrew RTL class timetable for grade י'2, semester א', used to find when a lesson occurs, who teaches it, where it meets, and any special instructions.","reading":"Readers scan from the right: first the merged day block, then the time, then subject/teacher/room as the lesson identity, and finally the notes as exceptions or instructions. Day rowspans group consecutive lessons, so those blocks must remain visually coherent.","groups":["יום + שעה — temporal anchors read first and define each rowspan block","מקצוע + מורה + חדר — the lesson's identity and location, compared across rows","הערות — secondary free-text annotations that can absorb wrapping"],"keep_intact":["time ranges such as 08:15–09:00","day labels ראשון, שני, שלישי","subject names","teacher names at least at word level","room numbers and room labels at word level"],"may_wrap":["הערות prose, which is long and naturally multi-line","multi-word room labels such as אולם ספורט at spaces","teacher full names at spaces only in a notes-priority design"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[62,110,84,89,97,277],"idea":"Balanced: every non-notes column stays on one line at its exact content width, and the remaining width goes to notes for moderate wrapping."},{"name":"B","widths":[70,120,95,100,114,220],"idea":"Schedule-first: give the day, time, subject, teacher and room columns extra breathing room for fast scanning, accepting a narrower notes column with more wrapping."},{"name":"C","widths":[62,110,84,63,67,333],"idea":"Notes-first: compress teacher and room to their minimum word-safe widths so the long הערות column gets nearly half the table width and wraps least."}]}
